To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SSQS proved to have good internal consistency and the SSQT and the SSQS were both related to health related quality of live outcome, but satisfaction with the social network was more relevant.
satisfaction with supportive interactions is an important predictor of health related quality life in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
the SSQS is a valid instrument for the measurement of support satisfaction, and that the SSQS and SSQT together explain a substantial amount of variance in health related quality of live measures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an instrument that can measure the two dimensions of social support.
the development and testing of the SSQS.
the development of a new instrument to measure social support and the satisfaction with supportive transactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SSQT, as a measure of supportive interactions, and the SSQS, as a measure for satisfaction with supportive transactions, are useful instruments in assessing social support and its impact on the health of RA patients.
the SSQS, in combination with the SSQT, is a valid instrument that measures the satisfaction with supportive interactions.
the SSQT measures the actual supportive transactions and the SSQS measures the satisfaction with the supportive transactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to get a complete picture of the social support provided to an individual, it is necessary to measure both supportive interactions and the satisfaction with these supportive transactions.

the SSQS is a useful instrument for assessing satisfaction with supportive transactions, and that the satisfaction with support provided is a relevant concept in the study of health related quality in life in RA patients.
, in addition to the number of supportive transactions, the satisfaction with the supportive transactions should be considered in the assessment of the quality of social support.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social support satisfaction is more important in predicting health related quality of live than supportive interactions.
satisfaction with social support is a relevant aspect of social support and should be measured in future research.
the two instruments are complementary and that the satisfaction with the provided support has more explanatory power in predicting health outcomes.
